## The estimation problem {.small}

- We observe an outcome $Y$, a binary treatment $D$ and covariates $X$, and we want the average treatment effect
  $$\theta_0 = \mathbb{E}\big[g_0(1, X) - g_0(0, X)\big], \qquad g_0(d, x) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid D = d, X = x].$$
- Double machine learning (DML) fits the outcome regression $g_0$ and the propensity score
  $m_0(x) = \mathbb{P}(D = 1 \mid X = x)$ on every new data set and combines them in the augmented inverse
  probability weighting (AIPW) score [@chernozhukov2018double; @robins1994estimation].
- AIPW is doubly robust: its bias is minus the inner product of the errors of the outcome regression and of the
  Riesz representer $\alpha_0(d, x) = d / m_0(x) - (1 - d) / (1 - m_0(x))$. Under overlap, cross-fitted AIPW gives
  valid confidence intervals at the parametric rate when the product of the two error rates is $o(n^{-1/2})$.
- The cost is a new round of model fitting and tuning for every data set.

## Prior-data fitted networks {.small}

- A prior-data fitted network (PFN) is a transformer pretrained on millions of tables simulated from a prior. On a
  new table it predicts in one forward pass, with the table as context and no fitting
  [@muller2022transformers; @hollmann2025accurate].
- Causal PFNs such as Do-PFN [@robertson2025dopfn], CausalPFN [@balazadeh2025causalpfn] and CausalFM
  [@ma2026causalfm] are trained end to end to output the effect directly.
- With fixed weights, a PFN is a statistical estimator [@nagler2023statistical]. Its effect estimate can carry a
  prior-induced confounding bias that more data does not remove [@melnychuk2026frequentist].
- The existing remedies correct the effect estimate, either on the posterior after pretraining or by changing the
  training labels or the prior [@melnychuk2026frequentist; @melnychuk2026debiased]. The network still hides the nuisances.

## Idea {.small}

- The simulator knows the exact nuisances of every task $\xi$: the propensity score $m_\xi$, the outcome regression
  $g_\xi$ and the Riesz representer $\alpha_\xi$. They are privileged information, available in training and never
  at deployment [@vapnik2009new].
- We supervise read-out heads of a small PFN with these noise-free nuisances.
- A parameter-free AIPW score layer combines the heads into the estimate
  $$\hat\theta = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \Big[\hat g(1, X_i) - \hat g(0, X_i) + \hat\alpha(D_i, X_i)\big(Y_i - \hat g(D_i, X_i)\big)\Big]$$
  with an influence-function standard error.
- The nuisances are outputs, and the correction is computed exactly from them, in context.

## Architecture {.small}

- **Backbones.** nanoTabPFN [@pfefferle2025nanotabpfn] and nanoTabICL [@qu2026tabiclv2], about 5 million
  parameters each, trained on one prior over a range of
  sample sizes (50 to 2,000 rows) and numbers of covariates (1 to 30).
- **Heads.** Read-out heads for $m$, $g$ and $\alpha$, and a CATE decoder whose mean gives the plug-in estimate.
- **Cross-fitting in context.** The rows are split into $K$ folds. Each fold is predicted with the other folds as
  context, so its nuisances never read its own rows. This costs $K$ forward passes and no training.
- **Variants.** V0 trains end to end on the effect, V1 adds the head losses, V2 trains through the score layer,
  and V3 anneals the head losses.

## Hypotheses {.small}

- **H1, training rate.** Supervising the nuisances reduces the synthetic tasks and the time needed to reach a fixed
  causal error.
- **H2, behavior out of prior.** The error of the score layer is governed by the product of its nuisance errors,
  and it degrades gracefully when one nuisance leaves the prior (weak overlap, strong heterogeneity, large effects,
  strong confounding).
- **H3, inference.** The influence-function intervals cover at fixed truths, and their coverage is compared with
  that of posterior credible intervals, including a credible interval trained with the label correction of [@melnychuk2026debiased].

## Study design {.small}

<!-- - **Pre-registered.** Every hypothesis, statistic, margin and outcome rule is fixed in a plan before the runs, and
  the plan is frozen by a tag. -->
- **Paired seeds.** Variants of one backbone share seeds, initialization and task streams, so each contrast is
  paired.
- **Two backbones.** A claim holds across architectures only if both families support it.
- **Fixed truths.** Bias and coverage are measured over 100 data sets per truth, in prior and in cells outside
  the prior.
- **Comparisons.** CausalPFN, CausalFM, Do-PFN, tuned DML [@bach2022doubleml], gradient-boosting learners and the
  post hoc correction of [@melnychuk2026frequentist].

## Contribution {.small}

- **Method.** A causal PFN whose nuisances are supervised outputs and whose estimate comes from an exact,
  cross-fitted AIPW layer, as an alternative to correcting the effect posterior.
- **Theory for trained networks.** In-context cross-fitting, Rao-Blackwellized supervision, and the result that
  the loss through the score layer does not identify the nuisances.
- **Evidence at scale.** A pre-registered test of training rate, behavior out of prior and coverage across two
  architectures, with a direct comparison of explicit and learned debiasing in a causal PFN.
